_readme: EDITABLE RULE REGISTRY for the deterministic linter (linter.py). Read by rules_engine.py.
* message  - the text shown to the user. {name} style tokens are filled in by the linter;
keep them if you want the dynamic value (e.g. the column or line number).
* enabled  - set to false to switch a rule OFF completely (its fix/warning is skipped).
* severity - advisory label only: critical | warning | fix | info.
* settings - shared constants; an 'env' var (if set in the environment) overrides 'value'.
* pattern  - fully data-driven: the engine runs the regex/fix from THIS file (custom_rules).
* builtin  - the detection/transform LOGIC lives in linter.py (see code_ref) because it is
too structural to express as a single regex. You can still edit its message,
toggle 'enabled', and tune any exposed params here.
ADD A NEW RULE: append an object to custom_rules (see the disabled examples there) and set
enabled=true. No Python changes needed. lang = sql | py | ksh | any.
DO NOT rename the 'id' fields of builtin rules — linter.py looks them up by id.

sql_dataset_map.description: Single source of truth for ${TEMPLATE_VAR}=RealDataset. The linter parameterizes each RealDataset to its ${VAR}; main.py resolves ${VAR} back to RealDataset. These MUST stay in sync. Format: VAR=Dataset,VAR2=Dataset2.

sql_param_columns.description: Comma-separated audit/batch columns that must always be parameterized to ${UPPER(name)} (e.g. etl_batch_sk -> ${ETL_BATCH_SK}). Empty disables.

env_path_segments.description: Path segments that should never be hardcoded; matched only as a complete /segment/ and rewritten to /${env}/. Affects both SQL string literals and KSH paths.

secrets.message: CRITICAL SECURITY ALERT: Found potential {name} in code. File processing halted.
secrets.description: Shift-left secret scan. {name} is the matched pattern's label from secret_patterns above. A hit halts all further processing of the file. Edit/add patterns in the secret_patterns block.

sql.message: Fix: Rewrote {n} NULL comparison(s) ('= NULL' / '!= NULL') to IS NULL / IS NOT NULL — '=' never matches NULL.
sql.description: Rewrites col = NULL / col != NULL to IS NULL / IS NOT NULL. {n} = number of comparisons rewritten.

sql.message: Fix: Removed doubled comma(s) in a column/value list.
sql.description: Collapses 'a,, b' to 'a, b'.

sql.message: Fix: Removed trailing comma before FROM (invalid in BigQuery).
sql.description: Removes a dangling comma immediately before the FROM keyword.

sql.message: Fix: Removed trailing comma before a closing parenthesis.
sql.description: Removes a dangling comma immediately before ')'.

sql.message: Fix: Parameterized hardcoded environment path segment(s) to '/${env}/'.
sql.description: Rewrites hardcoded env path segments (see settings.env_path_segments) inside SQL string literals to /${env}/.

sql.message: Critical: Unbalanced single quote detected — a string literal is missing its closing quote.
sql.description: Advisory only (cannot be auto-fixed): flags an odd number of single quotes.

sql.message: Fix: Parameterized hardcoded dataset '{real_ds}' to '{template}'.
sql.description: Replaces a hardcoded BigQuery dataset with its ${VAR}. {real_ds}/{template} come from settings.sql_dataset_map.

sql.message: Fix: Replaced 'TIMESTAMP()' with 'DATETIME()'.
sql.description: Converts TIMESTAMP(...) function calls to DATETIME(...).

sql.message: Fix: Corrected '{col}-<number>' (minus instead of equals) and parameterized to '{param}'.
sql.description: Fixes the common 'col-123' typo (minus used instead of '=') for a configured param column and parameterizes it. {col}=column, {param}=${COL}.

sql.message: Fix: Parameterized hardcoded '{col}' occurrences to '{param}'.
sql.description: Parameterizes a configured audit/batch column (settings.sql_param_columns) to ${COL}. {col}=column, {param}=${COL}.

sql.message: Fix: Merged multiple INSERT VALUES statements into a single batch statement.
sql.description: Collapses consecutive INSERT INTO <same table> VALUES statements into one multi-row INSERT.

sql.message: Fix: Removed a stray semicolon that incorrectly split a boolean/WHERE clause.
sql.description: Removes a ';' that wrongly split a statement before an AND/OR fragment.

sql.message: Warning: 'SELECT *' detected. Columns should be explicitly listed to prevent schema-drift errors.
sql.description: Flags SELECT * (advisory, no auto-fix).

sql.message: Warning: JOIN detected without an 'ON' condition. Verify this is not an accidental Cartesian product.
sql.description: Flags a JOIN with no ON/USING (and not an explicit CROSS JOIN).

sql.message: Critical Fix: Appended mandatory WHERE clause placeholder to a DELETE statement.
sql.description: Appends a <MISSING_FILTER_REQUIRED> placeholder to a DELETE with no WHERE. NOTE: the placeholder token itself is a code/main.py invariant and is not edited here.

sql.message: Critical Fix: Overwrote dangerous global bypass in DELETE statement with safe placeholder.
sql.description: Replaces WHERE TRUE / WHERE 1=1 in a DELETE with the safe placeholder.

sql.message: Critical Fix: Appended mandatory WHERE clause placeholder to an UPDATE statement.
sql.description: Appends a <MISSING_FILTER_REQUIRED> placeholder to an UPDATE with no WHERE.

sql.message: Critical Fix: Overwrote dangerous global bypass in UPDATE statement with safe placeholder.
sql.description: Replaces WHERE TRUE / WHERE 1=1 in an UPDATE with the safe placeholder.

sql.message: Fix: Extracted columns from SELECT and injected explicit Target Column List.
sql.description: For INSERT ... SELECT with no target column list, derives the list from the SELECT.

sql.message: Fix: Injected placeholder Target Column List ({val_count} cols) into INSERT for {table_name} — replace col1, col2… with the real column names.
sql.description: For INSERT ... VALUES with no target column list, injects col1..colN placeholders. {val_count}=column count, {table_name}=target table.

sql.message: Fix: Appended the missing statement-terminating semicolon to the final statement.
sql.description: Adds a trailing ';' to the last code line if missing.

schema.message: Fix: Corrected column name spacing to '{col}' using live schema.
schema.description: Uses the live BigQuery schema to rejoin a spaced column name (e.g. 'customer name' -> 'customer_name'). {col}=correct name.

schema.message: Fix: Collapsed an accidental space inside the column identifier '{w1} {w2}' -> '{w1}_{w2}'.
schema.description: Schema-independent: collapses a space inside an identifier sitting before a comparison operator. {w1}/{w2}=the two halves.

schema.message: Fix: Quoted string literal for STRING column '{col}' using live schema datatype.
schema.description: Quotes a bare literal compared against a STRING column. {col}=column name.

schema.message: Fix: Removed quotes around numeric literal for {ctype} column '{col}' using live schema datatype.
schema.description: Drops quotes around a numeric literal compared against a numeric column. {ctype}=datatype, {col}=column.

schema.message: Fix: Quoted date literal for {ctype} column '{col}' using live schema datatype.
schema.description: Quotes a bare date literal compared against a DATE/DATETIME/TIMESTAMP column.

schema.message: Fix: Removed quotes around BETWEEN bounds for {ctype} column '{col}' using live schema datatype.
schema.description: Normalizes quoted numeric bounds inside a BETWEEN range for a numeric column.

schema.message: Fix: Quoted BETWEEN date bounds for {ctype} column '{col}' using live schema datatype.
schema.description: Quotes bare date bounds inside a BETWEEN range for a date column.

schema.message: Warning: Column '{col}' is not in the live schema for this table — its filter was neutralized (TRUE). Verify the column name.
schema.description: WHERE-clause guard: a predicate column missing from the live schema is neutralized to TRUE and flagged. Only runs when a live schema was actually fetched.

schema.message: Fix: Wrapped STRING filter on '{ref}' with UPPER(TRIM()) for case-insensitive matching.
schema.description: Wraps a STRING-column filter predicate as UPPER(TRIM(col)) <op> UPPER(lit) for case-insensitive matching. {ref}=column reference.

py.message: Fix: Normalized inconsistent indentation so the module parses (statement re-aligned to its block level).
py.description: Only applied when the file does not compile AND the re-indented candidate does. Never reformats already-valid code.

py.message: Fix: Automatically appended mandatory '_VM' suffix to DAG_NAME.
py.description: Ensures DAG_NAME ends with the mandatory '_VM' suffix.

py.message: Fix: Injected missing 'timedelta' import into datetime module.
py.description: Adds timedelta to a 'from datetime import datetime' line when timedelta is used but not imported.

py.message: Fix: Removed 'catchup' from default_args (parameter belongs in DAG definition, not args).
py.description: Strips a 'catchup' key from default_args; the correct one is injected into DAG() (see py-inject-catchup).
Injects catchup=False into the DAG() call when absent. The injected token is a code invariant; edit message/enabled here.

py.message: Fix: Injected 'max_active_runs=1' concurrency limit into DAG definition.
py.description: Injects max_active_runs=1 into the DAG() call when absent.

py.message: Fix: Injected 'tags=["interface"]' array for workspace categorization.
py.description: Injects tags=["interface"] into the DAG() call when absent.

py.message: Fix: Updated stale job-ID prefix(es) {ids} to '{correct_id}' in variable names to match DAG_NAME.
py.description: Rewrites stale job-ID prefixes in variable/task names to match DAG_NAME's prefix. {ids}=sorted list found, {correct_id}=target prefix.

py.message: Warning: DAG defines no 'start_date' — Airflow requires one (set it in DAG() or default_args).
py.description: Advisory: a DAG with no start_date. No auto-fix (needs a human-chosen value).

py.message: Warning: DAG defines no schedule ('schedule_interval'/'schedule') — it will never run automatically.
py.description: Advisory: a DAG with no schedule. No auto-fix.

py.message: Warning: Bare 'except:' swallows ALL errors (incl. SystemExit) — catch specific exceptions instead.

ksh.message: Fix: Inserted missing '#!/bin/ksh' shebang at the top of the script.
ksh.description: Inserts a '#!/bin/ksh' shebang when the first line is not one. The shebang text itself is a code invariant.

ksh.message: Fix: Parameterized hardcoded environment path segment(s) to '/${env}/'.
ksh.description: Rewrites hardcoded env path segments (settings.env_path_segments) in non-comment lines to /${env}/.

ksh.message: Line {line:03d}: Forbidden raw 'bq query' invocation found. Refactored to wrapper.
ksh.description: Replaces a raw 'bq query' call with the enterprise execute_bq_wrapper. {line}=line number.

ksh.message: Line {line:03d}: Severe Security Breach. Masked explicit secret.
ksh.description: Masks an echoed password/secret/token literal. {line}=line number.

ksh.message: Line {line:03d}: Dangerous deletion pattern detected. Wrapped in safety check.
ksh.description: Wraps a 'rm -rf $VAR' in an emptiness guard so an unset variable can't delete '/'. {line}=line number.

ksh.message: Warning: Script lacks strict error handling. Injected 'set -e' and 'set -o pipefail'.
ksh.description: Injects 'set -e' and 'set -o pipefail' when neither is present.

ksh.message: Warning: 'execute_bq_wrapper' is called but its return code is never checked — add an RC=$? check after each execution.
ksh.description: Advisory: the BQ wrapper is invoked but '$?'/'RC=' is never inspected afterwards.

custom_rules.message: Warning: WITH (NOLOCK) is a SQL Server hint and is not valid in BigQuery — remove it.
custom_rules.description: EXAMPLE (disabled). Detection-only file-scope rule. Set enabled=true to activate. Copy this block to add your own.

custom_rules.message: Line {line:03d}: Use the logging module instead of print() in production DAGs.
custom_rules.description: EXAMPLE (disabled). Line-scope rule: reported once per matching line. {line} and {text} are available in the message.

EXAMPLE (disabled). Shows an auto-fix rule: the ordered 'fix' list applies regex search/replace to the file. A fix-only rule (no 'pattern') logs 'message' once when a fix actually changes the code. Add a 'pattern' if you want detection-only logging too.
